bio_en: Mihran Papazian studied in the Izmit region around 1910 with a classmate from Van, who remembered his broad chest, bright face and spellbinding speech. In 1912 the students secretly published the paper 'Paykar', and in 1914 he entered the Ottoman military school in Constantinople to become a non-commissioned officer. In 1923 he took refuge in Greece, first in Salonica and then Athens, where he held leading party posts. During the communist uprising in Athens he, his wife Arshaluys, their only son Sergo and the poet-teacher Manuk Manukian were treacherously murdered by Armenian communists; their bodies were found three weeks later in a pit.
notes: Compiled from the archive review, 2026-10-12. Confidence: medium. The text gives December 1944 in the editorial note and December 1945 in the biography; the Athens communist uprising was December 1944 - 1944 used, verify.
